technical_terms.how_marx_uses_it: Surplus-value is made through capital, and from surplus-value more capital is made.
Fewer holdings and more pasture turned a larger share of the total produce into surplus-produce.
The more empty the district is of men, the greater is its relative surplus population.
Capitalist accumulation presupposes a primitive accumulation that is its starting point, not its result.
Accumulation of capital presupposes surplus-value, which presupposes capitalistic production.
Owners of money seek to increase their values by buying other people's labour power.
Divorcing the producer from the means of production transforms the immediate producers into wage labourers.
Free labourers are not part of the means of production, nor do the means of production belong to them.
Owners of money, means of production and means of subsistence need free labourers to buy their labour power.
Flax used as raw material is transformed into an element of constant capital.
Variable capital preponderated greatly over constant in the early period.
In themselves money and commodities are no more capital than the means of production and subsistence.
Money is changed into capital, and capital is a social relation between persons, not a thing.
The expropriation of the agricultural producer from the soil is the basis of the whole process.
The expropriation of many capitalists by few is accomplished by the centralisation of capital.
Centralisation of the means of production and socialisation of labour become incompatible with their capitalist integument.
With the fall in numbers, rents and farmers' profits rose.
In England the industrial reserve recruits from the countryside, while in Ireland the agricultural reserve recruits from the towns.
Capitalist production creates wage-workers supernumerary in proportion to the accumulation of capital.
With such queer people, where is the field of abstinence for the capitalists?
The only part of national wealth that enters the collective possessions of modern peoples is their national debt.
In the colonies the labour-market is always understocked.
The expropriation and eviction of the agricultural population created the home-market.
Modern Industry alone supplies, in machinery, the lasting basis of capitalistic agriculture.
Manufacture, properly so called, conquers only partially the domain of national production.
The private property of the labourer in his means of production is the foundation of petty industry.
The east of England thrives on the so-called gang-system, a beautiful fruit of the vicious circle.
The agricultural revolution enriched the farmer just as speedily as it impoverished the agricultural people.
The system of protection was an artificial means of manufacturing manufacturers and expropriating independent labourers.
The subordination of labour to capital was only formal, since the mode of production had no specific capitalistic character yet.
In the 43rd year of her reign the nation was obliged to recognise pauperism officially.
Capital's aim is to transform the mass of the population into free labouring poor, an artificial product of modern society.

hegelian_or_philosophical.meaning_in_context: Capitalist production negates its own result, yielding individual property built on co-operation and common ownership.
The dispossession of the many by the few is reversed by the mass of the people.
The moments of primitive accumulation are its chief decisive factors.
Capital is not a thing but a social relation between persons, established through things.
Expropriation is done by the internal laws of capitalist production itself.
Labour is subordinated to capital in form only, before the mode of production acquires a specific capitalist character.
The monopoly of capital becomes a fetter upon the mode of production.
In the categoric sense, the farmer is an industrial capitalist too; industrial here is contrasted with agricultural.
Satire: in every sphere the lion's share falls to the middleman, even in religion through the Mediator and priests.

voice_attribution_risks.note: A gentleman's view that building brings poor is quoted; Marx's answer comes in later paragraphs.
Lord Dufferin's proposal is quoted, and the German 'Wie menschlich' is ironic, not Marx's approval.
A defender of enclosures is quoted against Dr. Price; the reader must not take his view as Marx's.
Eden's 'stoical peace of mind' is Marx's framing of Eden's conclusion, which is ironic.
A Tory's quote on wages is introduced as 'naïve'; Marx's ironic comment follows.
Mirabeau's praise of discrete workshops is quoted; footnote 4 explains Mirabeau's view as a product of its time.
Gülich's praise of Holland is quoted, then corrected by Marx in the same paragraph.
Wakefield's 'social contract' is quoted; the mockery belongs to Marx, not to Wakefield.
Molinari's footnote is quoted in French, followed by Marx's sarcastic 'How generous Mr. Molinari!'.

irony_examples.note: Original sin as an anecdote; 'Such insipid childishness' is Marx's mockery of Political Economy.
'Chevaliers d'industrie' rising by means as vile as those of a Roman freedman.
Eden's 'stoical' and 'comfortable' conclusion about the 'due proportion' of pasture.
'The smell of their fish rose to the noses of the great men' ironises the clan chiefs.
Deer 'demurely domestic cattle, fat as London aldermen' is a joke on the rich's hunting.
'In Japan, the circle of life-conditions moves more decently than this' is a sharp comparison.
Lord Dufferin is called a physician of the school of Sangrado, mocking his blood-letting plan.
'Rentroll's eyes' and 'l'appétit vient en mangeant' mock the landlord's endless demands.
'What grim irony!' on the beggar's licence for old men.
Footnote 4: 'can nothing now be done for the employed?' is a bitter aside.
Chapelier's claim that a coalition would restore the corporations is a pretext ironically exposed.
'Sweet commerce!' after the Dutch depopulation of Banjuwangi.
'Think of the horror!' ironises Wakefield's fear of losing imported workers.
'But, never mind, national wealth is ... identical with misery' is a bitter closing sarcasm.
'Tout sera pour le mieux dans le meilleur des mondes possibles' mocks the colonial scheme.

hard_passages.why: Dense: the double sense of 'free labourers' and the polarisation of the market.
Long Elizabethan Harrison quote in old spelling; Marx's Thornton remark is compressed.
Very long sentence on tenures, metayers and the farmer's rise.
Flax analogy: long sentence on constant capital and the 'new social soul'.
Abstract idea of usurer's and merchant's capital as capital quand même.
Long sentence on private property forms, ending in 'the expropriation of the mass of the people'.
Chain of negations and dialectical reversals; the 'expropriators are expropriated' turn.
Long sentence on relative surplus population, the labour-market and the Wakefield quote.
The 'sufficient price' argument: a long, ironic sentence that Marx leaves open to reading.
Long argument on the dull compulsion of economic relations versus direct force.
